title: Toyota FJ Cruiser
verdict: Toyota took the FJ40's face, bolted it to a Prado-family frame and gave it a rear locker. The blind spots are enormous and the back seat is for close friends only, but few new trucks of the 2000s went further off the pavement without a single aftermarket part.

paragraphs: The FJ Cruiser began as a show car. Toyota unveiled the concept, painted Voodoo Blue, at the Detroit auto show in January 2003, showed the production version at Chicago in February 2005, and had its subsidiary Hino Motors start building it at Hamura, Japan, in January 2006. Underneath was a ladder frame closely related to the Land Cruiser Prado's; on top sat a cartoon of the [[land-cruiser/fj40|FJ40]], white roof and all. America got it for model years 2007 through 2014. Other markets kept it until a 1,000-unit Final Edition for the Middle East closed out production in December 2022.

story.heading: A FORTY FOR A NEW CENTURY
paragraphs: By the time FJ40 production ended in 1984, the Land Cruiser had grown bigger and plusher. According to Larry Edsall's book on the truck, the idea of a new FJ with the old one's toughness came from product planner Dave Danzer and sales vice-president Yoshi Inaba in the mid-1990s. Danzer and Akio Toyoda quietly set up a shop at the NUMMI plant to test it, putting the bodies of Brazilian Toyota Bandeirantes, which descended from the FJ40, on Tacoma underpinnings. Toyota's Calty design studio in California then took over.

Inside Toyota the project was called the Rugged Youth Utility, aimed at young male buyers the company felt it was losing. Several concepts were tried before a retro design by Jin Won Kim, a 24-year-old Calty designer, won, with William Chergosky drawing the interior. The FJ40 cues are everywhere: a near-vertical windshield with three wipers, TOYOTA spelled out across the grille instead of the corporate badge, round headlights and a white roof. Rear-hinged access doors replaced the B-pillars, and high-strength steel took over their side-impact job.

story.heading: DEVELOPED ON THE RUBICON
paragraphs: From mid-2004 Toyota ran development mules over the hardest trails it could find, including Moab, the Angeles National Forest, the Mojave Desert and the Rubicon, and retuned the A-TRAC traction control and the suspension as a result. Underneath, the FJ shares hardware with the 120-series Prado, the [[4runner/4th-gen|4th-gen 4Runner]] and the [[lexus/gx470|GX 470]]: double-wishbone front suspension, a four-link coil-sprung rear axle with a lateral rod, and the 4.0-liter 1GR-FE V6. A 4x4 FJ has 9.6 inches of ground clearance and, Toyota says, can wade 28 inches of water.

The drivetrain choice is the interesting part. The six-speed manual came only with full-time 4WD: a Torsen center differential splits torque 40:60, locks at 50:50, and 3.909 axle gears give a 41.84:1 crawl ratio. The five-speed automatic got part-time 4WD, 3.727 gears and a 33.76:1 crawl ratio, and was also sold as a 4x2. Toyota's 2014 specifications list the rear electric locker as standard with the manual and optional with the automatic, and A-TRAC as part of an option package on 4x4s.

story.heading: THE PRICE OF STYLE
paragraphs: The styling that sold the truck also held it back. Reviewers praised its off-road ability and criticized its huge blind spots, small cargo area and cramped, awkward rear seat. Toyota added an optional backup camera for 2009 and new front-seat hinges for easier rear access in 2011. US sales fell from 56,225 in 2006 to 11,941 in 2009, and critics blamed rising fuel prices, more competition in the segment and the Jeep Wrangler.

Toyota's answer for 2010 was a dual VVT-i version of the 1GR-FE, with 259 hp on 87-octane fuel instead of 239 hp on 91, and slightly better economy. Early trucks also had a structural problem. The inner fender aprons in the engine bay of 2007 and some early 2008 trucks could bulge and crack, and Toyota changed the design. Owners still report cracked aprons on early trucks, so that's the first thing to look for when you open the hood.

story.heading: HOW IT ENDED
paragraphs: From 2008, Toyota built short runs of Trail Teams Special Editions, each in one color with blacked-out trim, TRD wheels and Bilstein shocks. On 5 November 2013 it announced that 2014 would be the last US model year, and the final Trail Teams truck became the Ultimate Edition: 2,500 built in Heritage Blue with a white grille surround, remote-reservoir rear Bilsteins, an aluminum front skid plate and, on automatics, CRAWL control. By the end of 2013, US sales alone had passed 200,000.

Production continued for other markets. Exports to Australia ended in August 2016, Japan got a Final Edition in September 2017 and stopped sales in January 2018, and the Middle East Final Edition closed production in December 2022. Toyota reused the name, though not the formula, for the 2026 Land Cruiser FJ, a smaller Hilux-based truck with a 2.7-liter four that isn't planned for North America. The original is now a collectible: on Bring a Trailer in late 2026, prices ran from $12,500 to more than $56,000.

callout.label: SIDEBAR · VOLUNTEERS WITH TOW STRAPS
callout.title: The FJ Cruiser Trail Teams
paragraphs: Before customers had their trucks, Toyota recruited volunteer Trail Teams from Toyota and Land Cruiser clubs. Paul Williamsen, Toyota's product education manager at the time, wrote that truck marketing manager Paul Czaplicki proposed the program in 2005, and that Bill Burke ran a week-long boot camp for the volunteers in Grand Junction, Colorado, in March 2006. Two of the volunteers he names drove [[land-cruiser/80-series|FJ80s]].

Each team drove two pre-production FJ Cruisers, towing enclosed trailers, to public trail events including Moab, Tellico and the Rubicon. They marked trails, gave first aid, recovered stuck vehicles, picked up trash and cooked camp meals until the passes snowed shut in November 2006. Toyota funded the program again for 2007 and 2008, and its success led to the Trail Teams special editions.

engineering_intro: The FJ Cruiser is a body-on-frame truck built from Toyota's mid-size Prado family of parts: independent double-wishbone front suspension, a four-link coil-sprung live rear axle and the 4.0-liter 1GR-FE V6. What's underneath depends on the gearbox. Manual trucks have full-time 4WD with a lockable Torsen center differential. Automatics have part-time 4WD, with an electric actuator that connects the front axle when you shift into four-wheel drive.

engineering.note: Similar, but not identical, to the two-door Prado's. Rear-hinged access doors and no B-pillar.
7.87 in front and 9.1 in rear wheel travel (2014 spec). Parts shared with the Prado 120, 4Runner, Tacoma and Hilux.
40:60 split, 50:50 locked. 3.909 gears for a 41.84:1 crawl ratio.
3.727 gears, 33.76:1 crawl ratio. Both transfer cases have a 2.566 low range.
239 hp / 278 lb-ft on 91 octane (2007–09). Dual VVT-i from 2010: 259–260 hp on 87.
Locker standard with the manual, optional with the automatic (2014 spec). 8-inch ring gears front and rear.

generations_table.note: Six-speed manual (full-time 4WD) or five-speed automatic (part-time 4WD or 4x2). Side curtain airbags standard from 2008.
Runs on regular. Trail Teams editions every year; CRAWL control on 2013–14 Trail Teams automatics.
3,200 built in Black Diamond with a black roof, TRD Bilsteins, rock rails, TRD wheels and BFGoodrich tires.
One monotone color a year: Iceberg (3,200), Sandstorm (1,500), Army Green, Radiant Red and Cement Gray (2,500 each). None for 2009.
2,500 in Heritage Blue with a white grille surround, remote-reservoir rear Bilsteins and a 1/4-inch aluminum skid plate.
Automatic 4x4 only in Australia and New Zealand. Plate on the rear bumper. Japan Final Edition in 2017.
Also sold in Chile, the Philippines and southern Africa. Middle East Final Edition limited to 1,000.

buying_checks.head: Get under it with a hammer and a light
buying_checks.body: Frame rust is the FJ's big weakness in salt-belt states. An IH8MUD member who shopped the Northeast said every truck he looked at had rot around the rear control-arm brackets or had already been patched. Another warned about rust hidden under thick fresh undercoating. Rust Buster's list of FJ repair sections (rail ends, center rails, crossmembers, coil buckets, body mounts) shows where to probe.

buying_checks.head: Open the hood and look at the inner fenders
buying_checks.body: The engine-bay inner fender aprons on 2007 and some early 2008 trucks could bulge and crack, and Toyota changed the design. Owners on IH8MUD report cracks that never grew and others that went all the way through. Look on both sides behind the headlights and price in a repair if they're split.

buying_checks.head: Check the rear access doors
buying_checks.body: The front seat-belt retractors are mounted in the rear-hinged access doors, and the door panels can crack after years of being slammed. Toyota recalled 2007–2013 trucks for it (NHTSA 13V098000). Run the VIN for open recalls and look at the inner door panels.

buying_checks.head: Feel for a clunk when it downshifts
buying_checks.body: A harsh jolt into first after sitting in Drive, as if you'd been rear-ended, is covered by Toyota bulletin T-SB-0046-12 for 2007–2013 FJ Cruisers and Tacomas. Greasing a dry rear driveshaft slip yoke often fixes it. Ask whether the driveshafts have been greased; Toyota calls for it every 5,000 miles on dirt, salt or when towing.

buying_checks.head: Manual trucks: listen at the clutch
buying_checks.body: A squeak or rattle from the gearbox that stops when you press the clutch is T-SB-0365-10 on 2007–2011 six-speed FJs: updated release bearing, fork support and release cylinder, with the transmission out. Manuals are much rarer than automatics, so expect to search harder.

buying_checks.head: Test every 4WD mode
buying_checks.body: Shift into 4H and 4L, try the rear locker and A-TRAC, and watch for warning lights that stay on. On automatic trucks the front axle is engaged by an electric disconnect actuator on the front differential; IH8MUD owners say they fail mostly from unsoldered internal contacts or water getting in.

buying_checks.head: Know which engine you're buying
buying_checks.body: 2007–2009 trucks make 239 hp and are rated on premium fuel; the dual VVT-i engine from 2010 makes 259–260 hp on regular. 4x2 automatics exist, so check the transfer-case lever. Trail Teams editions are monotone with blacked-out trim; confirm a claimed edition with the window sticker or a dealer build record.

buying_checks.head: Clear the smaller recalls too
buying_checks.body: 2014 trucks built 7–20 August 2013 need a new intermediate steering shaft (15V081000). Ultimate Editions had front lower ball-joint and lower-arm bolts checked for torque (14V539000). Trucks with the TRD brake kit or Toyota auxiliary driving lamps have their own campaigns.

repairs.title: Repair rotted rear frame sections
repairs.time: ≈ A weekend or more, with welding
repairs.cost: Rust Buster lists its rear rail kit at about $180 per side; welding labor extra
repairs.symptoms: Flaking, swollen or holed frame rails, rear control-arm brackets and crossmembers, often hidden under fresh undercoating on salt-belt trucks.
repairs.fix: Probe the rear frame, the lower-link brackets, the crossmembers and the coil-spring buckets with a hammer and pick. Wire-brush and treat surface rust; anything rotted through has to be cut out and replaced. Rust Buster makes FJ-specific caps for the last 28.75 inches of the rails and for the center rail section, plus crossmembers, coil buckets and body mounts shared with the 4Runner. All of them need welding. One IH8MUD owner replaced his rear lower-link frame brackets with Rust Buster pieces and added weld-on reinforcement.
repairs.tools: MIG welder · grinder and cutoff wheels · jack stands · rust converter · Rust Buster RB8432 (rear rail), RB8433 (center rail) and RB8427 (rear control-arm crossmember) as needed.

parts.name: Rear frame repair kit for 2007–2014 FJ Cruiser (RB8432)
Center frame repair kit for 2007–2014 FJ Cruiser (RB8433)
Rust Encapsulator & Internal Frame Coating Plus kit (inside and outside the rails)
Weld-through primer (coat the overlaps before you weld in patches)

repairs.title: Cure the downshift clunk at the rear driveshaft
repairs.cost: A tube of grease; a replacement rear driveshaft under T-SB-0046-12 was quoted at roughly $350–550
repairs.symptoms: A harsh jolt, as if you'd been rear-ended, when the transmission drops into first after the truck has been sitting in Drive. Toyota's bulletin covers 2007–2013 FJ Cruisers and Tacomas.
repairs.fix: Start with grease. A dry slip yoke binds and then lets go. Toyota's schedule says to lubricate the propeller-shaft spiders and slide yokes with lithium chassis grease, use molybdenum lithium grease on the double-cardan joint, and re-torque the shaft bolts. Do it every 5,000 miles if you drive on dirt or salted roads or tow. If the clunk survives a proper greasing and the driveshaft is confirmed as the cause, T-SB-0046-12 calls for a new rear driveshaft.
repairs.tools: Grease gun with a needle or angled coupler · lithium chassis grease · moly grease for the double-cardan · torque wrench.

repairs.title: Fix a failed front-axle disconnect actuator (automatic 4x4s)
repairs.cost: Free if you can solder; a replacement actuator costs more
repairs.symptoms: The transfer case goes into 4WD but the front wheels don't drive. The actuator may have water inside.
repairs.fix: On part-time trucks an electric actuator on the front differential slides a collar to connect the passenger-side axle when you shift into 4WD. IH8MUD member BMThiker says most failures come from internal contacts that only rest on their terminals; he opened the housing and soldered the motor and switch contacts. Water can also get in through a failed seal, a cracked housing or a damaged breather tube. On the trail, remove the actuator (a few 12 mm bolts), move the shift fork and slide the collar over by hand, then refit it to get 4WD back.
repairs.tools: 12 mm socket · soldering iron and solder · dielectric grease · tools to drop the skid plate if fitted.

repairs.title: Replace a front wheel bearing hub
repairs.cost: One IH8MUD owner paid about $85 for a Beck/Arnley assembly
repairs.symptoms: A growl or vibration from one front corner. One owner's bearing failed at 64,000 miles.
repairs.fix: Pull the dust cap and break the axle nut with a 35 mm socket and a long bar. Remove the caliper and rotor, then the four 17 mm bolts that hold the hub to the knuckle. Once they're cracked loose, switch to an open-end wrench, because the bolts can't back fully out with the hub in place. Knock the hub free and keep or replace the large O-ring behind it. A complete hub-and-bearing assembly bolts straight in, which saves you pressing a bearing without a 20-ton press.
repairs.tools: 35 mm socket · breaker bar · 17 mm open-end wrench · big hammer · torque wrench · new axle nut.

parts.name: Front wheel hub and bearing assembly, OEM (Prado/GX/FJ/4Runner)

repairs.title: Silence a squeaking clutch release bearing (six-speed)
repairs.cost: Was covered by the 5-year/60,000-mile powertrain warranty; now parts plus transmission labor
repairs.symptoms: A squeak or rattle from the transmission with the clutch pedal up that goes away when you press the pedal (2007–2011 FJ six-speeds).
repairs.fix: T-SB-0365-10: remove the release cylinder and the transmission, then fit the updated release cylinder, fork support and release bearing, inspect the clutch cover and reinstall. Order the bearing that matches the maker stamped on the edge of the clutch cover: Aisin 31230-60241 or LuK 31230-60231. The bulletin lists FJ release cylinder 31470-60361 and fork support 31236-35050. With the gearbox out, it's the time to fit a new clutch if it's worn.
repairs.tools: Transmission jack · 10 mm union-nut (flare) wrench · multi-purpose grease · Toyota repair manual.

repairs.title: Chop the front body mounts for bigger tires
repairs.cost: $34.95 for Metal Tech's plates, plus welding
repairs.symptoms: Oversize or wide tires rubbing at full lock or under compression, usually the inside of the tire hitting the front body mount.
repairs.fix: IH8MUD owners say rubbing on FJs is as much about tire width and wheel backspacing as diameter, and that the front body mount is the usual contact point at full lock. The fix is to cut the mount back and weld a cap over the opening. Metal Tech's laser-cut 3/16-inch plates show what to cut and come with instructions a welding shop can follow. Also remove or heat and reshape the plastic mud flap, which one owner found was the only thing his 285/70R17s touched on stock suspension.
repairs.tools: Cutoff wheel or plasma · welder · heat gun for the mud flap · primer and paint.

parts.name: Metal Tech FJ Cruiser body mount chop kit
Rust converter primer for the bare metal (RB9917)

repairs.title: Check, and live with or fix, cracked inner fender walls
repairs.time: ≈ 15 minutes to inspect · body-shop work to repair
repairs.cost: Free to inspect. A proper repair is body-shop labor, and Toyota's own fix meant pulling the dash and front end.
repairs.symptoms: A bulge, then a crack or tear, in the engine-bay inner fender aprons at the crumple zones, usually on both sides. 2007 and early-2008 trucks are the usual victims. Owners have filed dozens of NHTSA complaints. In the worst ones, the fenders dropped and bound on the doors or changed the door gaps.
repairs.fix: Open the hood and look along both aprons behind the headlights. If you see a bulge, scrape back the undercoating: one IH8MUD member's 'small bulge' turned out to be a crack once a Toyota factory rep cleaned it off. Plenty of cracks stop growing. One 2007 owner cracked his at 58,000 miles and traded the truck at 107,000 with little change, and another's grew slowly after a hard landing in a ditch. Toyota's warranty fix used redesigned aprons with support brackets welded inside, which meant removing the dash and front end. An IH8MUD member warned that welding sparks under the dash started a fire that destroyed one FJ, so any welder needs to strip or shield the dash first. For a truck with open cracks, have a body shop weld and reinforce the apron, then seal and paint it. With a heavy steel bumper and winch, avoid dropping the nose hard.
repairs.tools: Flashlight · plastic scraper · camera and tape measure to log crack length over time · for the repair: welder, weld-through primer, seam sealer, paint

repairs.title: Repair a chip before the windshield cracks
repairs.time: ≈ 30 minutes for a chip · replacement is a glass-shop job
repairs.cost: One IH8MUD member paid $50 for a chip repair. Early replacement quotes on IH8MUD ran about $1,600–1,800 with dealer glass.
repairs.symptoms: Chips from road debris that grow into long cracks, often from the bottom center of the glass. More than 60 NHTSA complaints across the 2007–2014 model years describe cracked FJ windshields, some after a pothole or cold weather and some from owners on their third or fourth windshield.
repairs.fix: The nearly upright glass takes the full force of every rock, so fix chips while they're small. A resin repair kept one IH8MUD member's small crack from spreading. If it has to be replaced, have the shop order a new top molding too. An IH8MUD member said it often gets ruined coming off; his dealer molding was about $278. Another member listed PPG FW02652 as the replacement glass. After a replacement, check for leaks at the top molding and A-pillars in the first rain or car wash.
repairs.tools: Windshield chip repair kit · glass cleaner · razor blade · UV light or sunshine to cure the resin

faq.q: What's the biggest tire I can fit without a lift?
faq.a: About a 285/70R17 (roughly 33 x 11 inches). One owner on stock suspension found his only rubbed the driver's-side mud flap under compression and fixed it by heating and flattening the flap. A long-time IH8MUD member's stricter view is that only a 31–32 inch tire clears in every situation; above that you need a body mount chop. Width and wheel backspacing matter as much as diameter, because the inside of the tire hits the front body mount at full lock.

With a 3-inch Old Man Emu lift, Slee Off-Road told one owner the limit is 285/70R17 unless you trim the body, and ARB told another 285/75R17. Several owners run 285/70R17s on factory wheels that way without rubbing. With the front body mounts chopped, owners run 305/70R17s, though one still rubs at full compression. One club's two FJs on 35s have trimmed body mounts and touch only at extreme flex and full lock.

They're different trucks underneath. The six-speed manual has full-time 4WD with a lockable Torsen center differential, 3.909 gears and a 41.84:1 crawl ratio. The five-speed automatic has part-time 4WD, 3.727 gears and a 33.76:1 crawl ratio. Toyota's 2014 specifications list the rear locker as standard on the manual and optional on the automatic. Manuals are much less common.

A rear electric locker, plus A-TRAC brake-based traction control in an option package on 4x4s. There's no factory front locker; one IH8MUD member fitted a Harrop E-Locker to his front diff. On very early trucks the rear locker could override A-TRAC. Toyota synchronized the two on the 2007 TRD Special Edition and in all production from November 2006.
Toyota originally rated the FJ at 5,000 lb for both 4x4 and 4x2. Under the SAE J2807 standard, the 2014 rating with the Class IV hitch was 4,700 lb.

faq.q: What fuel economy should I expect, and does it need premium?
faq.a: EPA ratings for 4x4s range from 14 city / 19 highway (2009 manual) to 17/21 (2010 automatic); a 2014 automatic is 17/20 and a manual 15/18. 2007–2009 trucks were rated on premium. The dual VVT-i engine from 2010 is rated on regular, although Toyota recommends premium for towing, off-roading and high altitude.

faq.q: Which years are the best to buy?
faq.a: 2010–14 if you can. Those trucks have the dual VVT-i engine on regular fuel, and CarGurus says the inner-fender bulge mostly shows up on 2007–09 trucks, while 2007 draws far more owner complaints than any other year. IH8MUD owners add that some pre-February 2007 builds had a brittle rear ring and pinion, so check the door-jamb build date. They also point out that an early truck you plan to re-gear anyway isn't much of a loss. Rust history and how the truck was used matter more than the year.

faq.q: What is the inner fender problem?
faq.a: The engine-bay inner fender aprons on 2007 and some early 2008 trucks could bulge and crack, and Toyota changed the design. Owners report everything from cracks that never grew to splits that went right through. Check both sides before you buy.

On IH8MUD's high-mileage thread, one Ontario owner passed 450,000 km (about 280,000 miles) on the original engine and transmission, and a Toronto owner reported 300k on a 2007 with one clutch replacement. Another member reports 250,000 miles of hard use without burning or leaking oil between oil changes.

faq.q: What were the Trail Teams editions?
faq.a: Monotone, black-trimmed, TRD-equipped FJs built in one color per year: Iceberg 2008 (3,200), Sandstorm 2010 (1,500), Army Green 2011, Radiant Red 2012 and Cement Gray 2013 (2,500 each), and the 2014 Heritage Blue Ultimate Edition (2,500). There wasn't one for 2009; a white TRD package filled the gap.

faq.q: Is the 2026 Land Cruiser FJ the same truck?
faq.a: No. The Land Cruiser FJ (J240) is a smaller Hilux-based truck with a 2.7-liter four-cylinder and a six-speed automatic, built in Thailand from 2026. Toyota hasn't planned it for North America or Europe.

mods.why: A 2.5–3 inch lift with better shocks clears 285/70R17s on factory wheels. Kits are split by 2007–09 and 2010–14 trucks, so buy for your year.

baseline_service.intro: Assume nothing has been done, and assume the driveshafts have never seen grease. Intervals below come from Toyota's 2011 FJ Cruiser Warranty & Maintenance Guide; capacities come from AMSOIL's lookups for 2011 and 2007 trucks. Specs changed in 2010 (0W-20 oil, larger oil capacity, 75W-85 diff oil), so check your owner's manual for 2007–2009 trucks.

items.spec: SAE 0W-20 (2010–14) · ≈6.4 qt with filter; 2007–09 ≈5.5 qt (AMSOIL lists 5W-30) · drain plug 30 ft-lb
items.interval: Every 10,000 mi / 12 months on 0W-20; every 5,000 mi / 6 months on dirt roads, when towing or carrying heavy loads (Toyota)
items.note: If the last change wasn't 0W-20, Toyota says to change it again at 5,000 miles.

items.interval: Replace every 30,000 mi; inspect every 5,000 mi on dirt or dusty roads (Toyota)
items.note: Check the airbox seal while you're there.

items.interval: Replace every 30,000 mi (Toyota); sooner in dust or heavy traffic
Every 120,000 mi (Toyota); replace at purchase if the history is unknown near that mileage

items.spec: Toyota Super Long Life (pink) or equivalent non-silicate, non-amine, non-borate HOAT · ≈10.4 qt (auto) / 9.9 qt (manual)
items.interval: First at 100,000 mi / 120 months, then every 50,000 mi / 60 months (Toyota)
items.note: Inspect hoses and connections for corrosion and leaks at the same time.

items.spec: Toyota ATF WS · ≈11 qt total fill, ≈3.2 qt per drain-and-fill
items.interval: Toyota lists replacement at 60,000 mi only for towing or heavy loads, otherwise inspection. Drain and fill at purchase if there's no record.
items.note: A drain-and-fill replaces only part of the fluid; repeat it rather than pressure-flushing.

items.spec: 75W-90 GL-4 or GL-5 · ≈3.8 pt · drain and fill plugs 27 ft-lb
items.interval: Replace every 30,000 mi when towing or heavily loaded (Toyota); otherwise inspect
items.note: Change it at purchase on a manual truck with no records.

items.spec: Toyota transfer gear oil, grade [CONFIRM IN MANUAL] · ≈2.1 pt part-time (auto), ≈3 pt full-time (manual), per AMSOIL's 2007 listing
items.interval: Replace every 30,000 mi on dirt roads or when towing (Toyota); otherwise inspect

items.interval: Replace front and rear every 15,000 mi when towing or heavily loaded (Toyota); otherwise inspect

items.interval: Every 5,000 mi on dirt roads, salted roads or when towing, with a propeller-shaft bolt re-torque (Toyota)
items.note: Dry slip yokes cause the downshift clunk. See the driveshaft repair above.

items.item: Brake fluid (and clutch fluid on manuals)
items.interval: Toyota lists clutch-fluid replacement every 30,000 mi for trucks used daily off-road at high rpm and low speed; otherwise inspect. Flush both at purchase if there's no record.

items.note: Look for wet hoses at the pump and rack.
